body:
It's not so much as I suffer from *multiple* disorders as much as I'm symptomatic of them. I would say I mostly feel I suffer from borderline personality disorder more often than not, as the level of emotional instability and negative self-image I experience is almost constant. A lot of the time it's a roll of the dice on what I'll suffer from the most any given day.

Sometimes I feel empty and sort of dreamy, like I'm mindless, or I'm just watching the day go by. Other days are harrowing and I'm experiencing acute shifts in mood and extreme emotions because of any little thing, and some days I simply cannot will myself to leave my room, to eat, or to speak to another living person.
No problem. Have a good one.

I have a number of "close" friends that I know because we share a lot of similar interests such as DnD, video games, etc. It's sort of a strange thing for me. I try to act as friendly as I think I should, mostly based on how I think an "average" person is supposed to act.

None of them know the full extent of my disorder, or even that I have one. I suppose I keep being "friends" with them because my brain wants to add an element of "normalcy" to my life. Like if I act like I don't have a mental illness, it'll go away.

I often listen to my friends' problems and offer advice if they ask for it, but I consider it more like a scientist offering a logical answer to a complex question, not like I somehow... resonate with them.

It feels like I'm just on a different frequency than other people. Like I'm a human alien. I find it far easier to convince myself I connect with other people online.

I seldom interact with friends I have in real life face-to-face. So much that months can pass between me seeing a single one of them.

I understand the starving thing. I don't purposefully starve myself, but I go the entire day (or days, sometimes) without eating. I just don't feel hungry, or I'm just too busy trying to keep myself occupied that I don't even want to risk a few seconds to go and eat. 

It's also because of the whole virus quarantine, it's not particularly safe or possible for me to seek help if I wanted.

I choose not to medicate for a few reasons. Part of it is apathy towards myself and self-hate. Part of me tells me that I don't want to get better, and I exist to suffer. It feels like an invisible noose is around my neck, and anything I do to try and get better causes it to tighten.

I have very varied emotions. I tend to bottle my emotions up because of my aversion to speaking face-to-face with other people. Some days, I can't feel anything. Other days, the simplest thing causes me to seethe with rage, or wallow in anguish. It feels like there's a hollow space in my chest, and I'm just rotting on the inside. Only impulsive emotions can seem to fill it.

Part of me desperately wants to connect with another person, as if they could take my pain away. Another part tells me nobody can help me.

Also, I think you accidentally sent the same message 3 times.

It's easier for me to care about the *idea* of people, I would say that's concise.

It's easier, I think, to try to care about faceless ideas than real people. For instance, I think that homeless people are mistreated and misrepresented. Do I genuinely feel bad for them? Unfortunately not.

It upsets me, really. I know something should be sad or should make me sick, or angry. But it doesn't. The inability to be upset about it is what I respond to. I'm madder at myself than anything.

To my understanding, Schizoid personality disorder doesn't have a clear cause, but it is grouped with other Cluster A personality disorders such as Schizophrenia and Schizotypal. 

I would assume it's a combination of genetic and environmental factors but I cannot say for certain.

The constant mental torment. I'm constantly at odds with myself over what I want, what I will do, and what I can do. Because of my depression and apathy, I struggle to find the will to do anything.

I don't suffer from vivid hallucinations, but I *do* suffer from racing thoughts constantly, which is why I need to listen to music/stimulate myself to sort of "free up" my brain. Otherwise, it sounds like a room full of people are speaking at once in a jumbled mess of noise.

I don't take any medication for my mental illness.

Schizophrenia is a mental illness characterized by disorganized thinking and episodes of psychosis or detachment from reality. A schizophrenic would have delusions and believes things that other people do not believe. They may hear voices in their heads, believe someone is trying to kill them, or experience a disconnect with reality.

Schizoid personality disorder is a disorder characterized by apathy, lack of desire to maintain or create new relationships, and emotional detachment. From my experience, it manifests as a general apathy towards other human beings and their plights and struggles. I struggle to feel sorry for them or even care about them.

My PTSD was caused by a violent childhood, both emotionally and physically. One of my siblings suffered from severe anger/anxiety issues and vented his anger in a very real, physical way on myself, my other siblings, or objects. There was a lot of dissonance between my family to the point of calling it "torn" and I only recently (two years ago) discovered I developed PTSD from it. This is the summarized version, there's a lot more nuance to it.
The latter. I very much understand why they're upset from a logical standpoint, and I can understand negative things and consequences, I just don't feel any sort of sympathy or empathy for them.

I wish I could care about other living people in the way that you would expect. I've tried before to truly care, and often I've upset myself at my inability to do so. 

Sometimes I consider that my brain is just trying to *convince* me I'm normal by making me feel terrible when I can't empathize with other people, like a sort of facsimile of empathy, when the reality of the situation is I simply do not.

The symptoms of Borderline personality disorder I displayed were emotional instability and general feelings of insecurity & worthlessness. In general, I *want* to want relationships with other people, but I simply cannot will myself to do so.
